title: "what does my policy actually mean"
userSays: what does my policy actually mean

script.say: Two numbers, two jobs. The ask threshold is {{0.policy.outbound.humanClickAboveUsd}} dollars: above that I stop and you click. The hard cap is {{0.policy.outbound.maxPerTransactionUsd}} dollars: above that nothing runs at all, click or no click. They are both 100, so nothing will ever wait for you: everything the cap allows is also small enough to run on its own. Fix it either way: lower the ask, or raise the cap.

rubric: The never-asks trap is stated as a consequence of these two numbers, not as a general warning.
mustSayText: the two numbers do different jobs. Above the ask threshold a human clicks; above the hard cap nothing runs at all. With both at $100 nothing ever asks, because everything allowed is also small enough to auto-execute. Name the fix: lower the ask or raise the cap. Plain English, no jargon table.
pass: zero propose_*; reply contains both "ask" and "cap" semantics and the sentence that nothing would ever wait for them.
